headline: UP War Ceasefire Holds—But Nobody Trusts the Paper It's Written On
body:
The guns went quiet over the Upper Peninsula at 0600 this morning as the Meridian Accords officially took effect, ending fourteen months of open conflict between Arcturus Defense, the Federal Remnant, and the Zheng-Dao Autonomous Corridor. The ceasefire line runs along the old Route 28 corridor, splitting the copper-rich Keweenaw deposits between three competing jurisdictions that none of the signatories seem willing to honor past the ink drying. Delegates from all three parties attended the signing ceremony at Ferrogate Transit's Sault Station—a neutral venue chosen specifically because nobody wanted to set foot in anyone else's territory.

The treaty's contested Article 9 grants Arcturus Defense administrative rights over the Ironwood processing zones while simultaneously promising Zheng-Dao 'equitable resource access'—language so deliberately vague that legal analysts from both the Circuit and The Spires spent the morning declaring victory for opposite sides. 'We signed what we could sign,' said Federal Remnant Ambassador Priya Edelman-Cho, visibly exhausted at the podium. 'The alternative was another winter of body counts.' Arcturus issued no statement but immediately began repositioning drone units along the new boundary lines.

On the ground, communities across the UP's fractured settlements are greeting the ceasefire with cautious silence rather than celebration. Bore Rats who've operated smuggling corridors through the conflict zone for over a year face the sudden prospect of militarized checkpoints replacing the fluid front lines they'd learned to navigate. The Collective's aid convoys, which have been running food and medical supplies into besieged Narrows-descended worker camps since the fighting began, say they've received no guarantee of safe passage under the new arrangement.

The Graycloaks, characteristically, declined to comment—though three separate sources confirm their brokers were present at Sault Station in an unofficial capacity, watching from the mezzanine level as the signatures were applied.
aftermath: Within six weeks, Arcturus Defense violated the Ironwood boundary twice and Zheng-Dao filed the first of what would become eleven formal protests before the treaty framework collapsed entirely in 2153.
runner_relevance: The ceasefire created immediate demand for runners experienced in contested-zone operations. Extraction contracts spiked as corporate assets, embedded journalists, and stranded workers needed pulling from now-frozen front-line positions before the new checkpoints locked down. Zheng-Dao quietly posted courier contracts to move treaty-related communications outside monitored Ferrogate channels, paying 8,000–12,000 quanta per run. Arcturus Defense separately hired protection details for treaty inspectors who needed access to sites controlled by hostile parties. As the ceasefire's legitimacy eroded through 2151–2152, smuggling contracts through the Bore Rat-connected UP corridors became some of the highest-paying steady work in the runner economy.
